newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures limit-up in late trading.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures limit-up in late trading.

text.p: CME lumber futures posted limit gains in January and March contracts in reaction to higher cash lumber prices, active home sales and a severe snowstorm in the Pacific Northwest, traders and analysts said.

Traders said cash spruce prices were trading from $400 to $405 per tbf Monday, versus quotes Friday at $392. A 1.8 percent jump in existing home sales in November to 4.04 million units, according to the National Association of Realtors, also was seen as bullish.
Some analysts said the snowstorm pounding the Pacific Northwest and British Columbia was seen as bullish because it may force production cutbacks at sawmills there.
At 1200 CST, lumber was up $10.00 to down $0.10 with January and March limit-up at $414.70 and $407.30.
